clue.text: Stop an income like this? Then claim some!

definitions.text: Stop an income like this? Then claim some!

parts.words: Stop an income like this? Then claim some!
parts.note: if someone cuts off your earnings in this way, you are entitled to demand money back to make good the loss

explanation.surface: An indignant call to sue anyone who cuts off your earnings.
explanation.definitionFit: Payment made to make good a loss, such as lost earnings, is exactly what you would claim.

clue.text: Young birds cry heartlessly to drunken gents

indicators.note: without its heart, the middle letter of the word cry is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before its centre is removed

indicators.note: drunk people stagger about, so the letters of gents are jumbled

explanation.surface: Baby birds squawk with their beaks half shut at some tipsy men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' removes R from CRY to leave CY; 'drunken' rearranges GENTS into GNETS.
explanation.definitionFit: A young swan is called by this name, so the plural is young birds.

clue.text: Kisses won't start, but strolls around can begin

indicators.note: the word for kisses loses its opening letter

parts.note: smooches are kisses, an informal word

explanation.surface: A courtship stalls at kissing, but the couple can at least go for a walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'won't start' takes the S off SMOOCHES; 'but' and 'can begin' only pad the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To mooch is to wander or loaf about aimlessly, a synonym of strolling around.

clue.text: Wild rose in a gentle setting

indicators.note: a fresh setting rearranges the letters of in a gentle

explanation.surface: A wild rose growing in a gentle garden setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting' rearranges the nine letters of IN A GENTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is another name for sweetbriar, a species of wild rose.

clue.text: Retreat following old army girls and workers

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the letters for the old army girls are read in reverse

parts.note: the ATS, Auxiliary Territorial Service, was the British women's army corps in the Second World War
ff. is the abbreviation for following, as in following pages

explanation.surface: Wartime women soldiers and labourers pulling back together.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm's staff is its body of employees, the people who work there.

clue.text: Isolde's lover is no longer in transit

indicators.note: the letters are no longer arranged as they were in the word transit, so they are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Isolde's lover has finally arrived after his journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no longer in' tells you to rearrange TRANSIT. In the medieval legend, Tristan and Isolde are tragic lovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tristan is the knight who loves Isolde in the Arthurian romance and Wagner's opera.

clue.text: Spontaneous behaviour means nothing for every worker

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means nothing
per means for each or for every, as in miles per hour
an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: A remark that acting on impulse brings no reward to any employee.
explanation.definitionFit: In psychology, operant behaviour is action emitted spontaneously rather than triggered by a stimulus.

clue.text: Irate nobleman takes railway through fields and woods

parts.note: cross means angry or irate
a count is a nobleman

explanation.surface: An angry aristocrat boards a train to travel through the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-country route runs over open land rather than along roads.

clue.text: Newspaper has a party by the lakes that is for a child

parts.note: a rag is slang for a low-quality newspaper
a do is an informal party
L is the map abbreviation for lake, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A tabloid holds a children's party beside the Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft cloth toy figure is a plaything made for a child.

clue.text: A food flavouring: one is in demand

parts.note: A, the indefinite article, means one

indicators.note: is placed within the word for demand

parts.note: need means demand or requirement
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that a particular flavouring is currently popular.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'A' belongs to the definition; the A in the answer comes from 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: The seed of the anise plant is used to give a liquorice flavour to food.

clue.text: Obvious villain gets right among the racehorses horses

parts.note: a demon is a wicked person, a villain

indicators.note: the letter for right goes amid the letters of the word for racehorses

parts.note: a stable is a set of racehorses kept by one owner or trainer

explanation.surface: A rogue is caught among the runners at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as published repeats 'horses' after 'racehorses', an apparent slip with no job in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Something demonstrable can be clearly shown, so it is evident or obvious.

clue.text: King of horror stories: he spent wildly

indicators.note: wild behaviour scatters things, so the letters of he spent are rearranged

explanation.surface: A best-selling horror writer squandered his fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' rearranges HE SPENT. The definition means the novelist Stephen King, not a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen King is the famous American author of horror novels, so his first name is meant.

clue.text: Heavy work might make you healthier

parts.note: fat means heavy or overweight
to farm is to work the land

explanation.surface: Strenuous labour can improve your health.
explanation.definitionFit: A health resort where overweight people go to slim is meant to improve their wellbeing.

clue.text: Puts a price on lettuce with a stone in it

indicators.note: the stone goes inside the lettuce

parts.note: cos is a type of lettuce, also called romaine
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: A grocer prices a lettuce that has a pebble inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To cost something is to estimate or fix its price.

clue.text: I must have support, not changing direction, in London

parts.note: a sling is a support for an injured arm

indicators.note: going the other way, so the word not is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone in London insists on support while staying on course.
explanation.definitionFit: Islington is a borough of north London, so it is a place in the capital.

clue.text: The woolly wanderer? Behold! She must get into step!

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

indicators.note: she is placed inside the word step

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A command to a straying woman to fall into line.
explanation.definitionFit: A stray from the flock is a woolly animal that has wandered off, as in the parable.

clue.text: They disturb jumping dogs

parts.note: up suggests leaping, as in jumping up
setters are gun dogs

explanation.surface: Dogs leaping about cause a disturbance.
explanation.definitionFit: People or things that upset others disturb them.

clue.text: Identity tag for tea provider in uniform

indicators.note: the tea provider goes inside the word for uniform

parts.note: same means uniform, unvarying
an urn is a large vessel for serving tea

explanation.surface: A name badge for the person serving tea in uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: A family name is the label that identifies a person.

clue.text: Slyly thieve a pound; that's sister's job

indicators.note: a sly arrangement is a crafty one, so the letters of thieve are moved around

parts.note: L, from Latin libra, is the symbol for a pound

explanation.surface: A nun sneakily pockets some money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slyly' rearranges THIEVE into THEVEI. To take the veil is to become a nun, a religious sister.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun's veil is the mark of her vocation, so it stands for a religious sister's calling.

clue.text: Overturn potato turnover

indicators.note: turning the word over reads its letters backwards

parts.note: a potato is a tuber

explanation.surface: A pastry turnover filled with potato is knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' looks like a pastry, but it reverses TUBER.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebut a claim is to refute it, overturning the argument.

clue.text: It goes round, up and down

indicators.note: in a down entry the letters read the same whether going up or down the grid

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A spinning thing that moves up and down as it turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotator is a device or part that rotates, turning round.

clue.text: Smeared bishop kept inside by wretched daughter

indicators.note: the bishop's letters are held within the word for wretched

parts.note: blue means miserable or wretched
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A disgraced bishop is held captive by his unhappy daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: Bishop is usually B, but here it is RR (Right Reverend), placed in BLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A smeared image is blurred, its outlines smudged and unclear.

clue.text: The sailor has ambitions

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
gets means obtains or has

explanation.surface: A sailor with big plans.
explanation.definitionFit: Goals or aims are the things one is ambitious to achieve.

clue.text: Spades used on verge that is like grass

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for spades in card games
the edge of something is its verge

explanation.surface: Gardening spades used to trim a grass verge.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedges are grasslike plants of marshy ground, resembling grass.

clue.text: Fruit one has to like if on the turn

indicators.note: turning round, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: A means one
must means has to
as means like

explanation.surface: Someone has to enjoy a fruit, even one going off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the turn' reverses AMUSTAS as a whole. 'On the turn' also suggests fruit going bad.
explanation.definitionFit: A satsuma is a kind of small loose-skinned mandarin orange.

clue.text: April 5: what does Ray need badly?

indicators.note: something done badly is mangled, so the letters of Ray need are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about what a man called Ray really requires on a spring day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges RAY NEED. In Britain the tax year ends on 5 April.
explanation.definitionFit: The British financial or tax year finishes on 5 April, so that date closes the year.

clue.text: Win during the seventh rally

indicators.note: the answer runs within the words seventh rally

explanation.surface: A victory in the seventh exchange of a tennis match.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthral someone is to captivate or win them over.

clue.text: Having a cheerful disposition, like Bach's clavier?

definitions.meaning: Bach wrote a famous set of keyboard pieces for an instrument tuned in equal temperament

explanation.surface: A genial person compared to Bach's keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means even-tempered and also names Bach's keyboard collection, tuned to a tempered scale.
